title: B2B SaaS Dashboard Usability Checklist
desc: Ensure your data visualization, summary metrics, and operational cards empower user action instead of cognitive fatigue.
lead: A practical evaluation guide for software dashboards to balance high data density with effortless glanceability.

items.title: Above-the-fold core metric cards
items.desc: Are the top 3-4 vital health metrics immediately visible without scrolling?

items.title: Contextual delta badges
items.desc: Does every KPI show comparison context (e.g., +12% vs last month) with color coding?

items.title: Logical reading flow
items.desc: Are high-level summaries at the top and detailed tables placed below?

items.title: Zero decorative chart clutter
items.desc: Are 3D graphs, superfluous gradients, and decorative background lines removed?

items.title: Accessible color palettes
items.desc: Can charts be distinguished by color-blind users and in grayscale?

items.title: Hover inspection tooltips
items.desc: Do chart hover tooltips display precise values, timestamps, and segment names?

principles: If a metric doesn't prompt an action when it turns red, it does not belong on the main dashboard view.
Never truncate numbers arbitrarily: use clear suffixes like $1.4M with full precision on hover.

faqs.q: How many widgets should be on a single dashboard screen?
faqs.a: Limit primary dashboard views to no more than 6-8 core widgets. Group secondary metrics into specialized tabbed sub-views.

title: Design Token Architecture & Hand-Off Guide
desc: The complete blueprint for structuring design tokens, naming conventions, and Tailwind configuration contracts.
lead: Learn how to build a unified design system where every Figma style maps 1:1 to Tailwind CSS classes and TypeScript tokens.

items.title: Tier 1: Primitives
items.desc: Raw values (e.g., obsidian-950: #090b07, lime-400: #d0ff58) with zero semantic meaning.

items.title: Tier 2: Semantics
items.desc: Contextual aliases (e.g., bg-canvas: obsidian-950, text-accent: lime-400, border-subtle).

items.title: Tier 3: Component Tokens
items.desc: Scoped component styling (e.g., btn-primary-bg, card-surface-hover).

items.title: Automated WCAG contrast check
items.desc: Do all text and surface token pairs exceed 4.5:1 contrast ratios?

items.title: Explicit focus visible tokens
items.desc: Are focus rings standard, high contrast, and offset from dark surfaces?

items.title: Zero arbitrary magic numbers
items.desc: Are all padding, margins, and radii values locked to the 4/8px token ladder?

principles: Tokens represent decisions, not just hex codes. Changing a token updates your entire product consistently.
Keep primitive palettes small: having 15 different shades of gray is a failure of constraint.

faqs.q: Should tokens be stored in Figma or code?
faqs.a: Code is the final source of truth. We export design tokens from code (TypeScript/JSON) into Figma variables to maintain absolute parity.

title: Heuristic Evaluation Scorecard & Template
desc: The exact heuristic framework, severity scorecard, and presentation structure I use for $499 client audits.
lead: Evaluate your digital product through Jakob Nielsen's 10 Heuristics combined with modern SaaS behavioral psychology models.

items.title: P0 — Blocker (Conversion Killer)
items.desc: Users cannot complete transaction, signup, or primary workflow; immediate loss of revenue.

items.title: P1 — High Friction
items.desc: Users can complete the task but experience severe hesitation, confusion, or retry loops.

items.title: P2 — Moderate Inconsistency
items.desc: Visual drift, misalignment, or slow interaction patterns that reduce brand perceived trust.

items.title: P3 — Low Cosmetic
items.desc: Minor typographic or spacing imperfections that do not impair workflow completion.

items.title: Visibility of System Status
items.desc: Does the system always keep users informed about what is going on through appropriate feedback?

items.title: Match Between System and Real World
items.desc: Does the interface speak the user's language rather than internal engineering database terms?

items.title: User Control and Freedom
items.desc: Do users have clear emergency exits to leave unwanted states without an extended dialogue?

items.title: Error Prevention Over Error Messages
items.desc: Does the design eliminate error-prone conditions before they occur?

principles: Always prioritize P0 conversion blockers before spending time polishing minor P3 styling details.
Record your audit walkthrough via video: hearing vocal hesitation illustrates friction far better than static screenshots.

faqs.q: Can I use this template to audit my own product?
faqs.a: Yes, though founders often suffer from 'creator blindness'. Having an external expert walk through your flow uncovers assumptions you take for granted.

title: 50-Point SaaS UX Launch & Audit Checklist
desc: A battle-tested 50-point checklist covering onboarding, navigation, tables, forms, and mobile heuristics for SaaS founders and engineers.
lead: Before deploying your next release or product launch, run your screens through this exhaustive checklist to catch silent conversion killers and usability traps.

items.title: Single-field initial signup
items.desc: Is signup reduced to just email and password without upfront company size or role questions?

items.title: Sub-3-minute Time-to-Value
items.desc: Can a user experience the core product value before seeing a billing prompt?

items.title: Interactive starter templates
items.desc: Are new accounts pre-populated with realistic sample data instead of blank empty states?

items.title: Deferred workspace invites
items.desc: Is team member invitation suggested AFTER the initial user experiences value?

items.title: Active route highlighting
items.desc: Does the sidebar or navbar clearly indicate the current screen with high contrast?

items.title: Breadcrumb hierarchy
items.desc: Can users traverse 2+ levels deep back to parent collections with 1 click?

items.title: Global search (Cmd + K)
items.desc: Is keyboard-navigable search available across entities and settings?

items.title: Back button fidelity
items.desc: Does clicking browser back return to the previous view without resetting active filters?

items.title: Inline validation on blur
items.desc: Do inputs validate after the user unfocuses rather than waiting for form submission?

items.title: Destructive action confirmation
items.desc: Do deletions require explicit typed confirmation or 2-step modal prompts?

items.title: Autofocus on primary input
items.desc: Does the first form input receive focus automatically upon screen load?

items.title: Helpful error recovery copy
items.desc: Do error messages explain HOW to fix the issue instead of just saying 'Invalid input'?

items.title: Sticky header rows
items.desc: Do table column headers remain visible during vertical scrolling?

items.title: Visible sorting indicators
items.desc: Is active sort column and direction clearly badged with SVG arrows?

items.title: Clear filter badge counts
items.desc: Does the filter trigger display active filter count and 1-click 'Clear All'?

items.title: Row hover contrast
items.desc: Do table rows highlight clearly on hover for scannability?

principles: Fixing onboarding friction yields 3x higher impact on ARR than tweaking checkout button colors.
Never present a user with an empty state without an immediate primary action to populate it.
Make destructive actions hard to trigger accidentally, but trivial to undo.

faqs.q: How often should my team review this checklist?
faqs.a: Run this checklist before any major product version launch, or at the end of each monthly development cycle.
